simple.meaning: רָפַשׂ (râphas) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to trample , i.e. roil water.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Proverbs, Ezekiel, beginning at Proverbs 25:26. The surrounding contexts include family line, death, kingship, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָפַשׂ (H7515) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: רָפַשׂ (râphas) / H7515 is traced through Proverbs 25:26, Ezekiel 32:2, Ezekiel 34:18 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: Like a muddied spring and a polluted well,
‘Son of man, take up a lamentation over Pharaoh king of Egypt, and tell him,

Does it seem a small thing to you to have fed on the good pasture, but you must tread down with your feet the residue of your pasture? And to have drunk of the clear waters, but must you foul the residue with your feet?
